stem: A client who uses an insulin pump is preparing for air travel. Which statement shows correct understanding of insulin and pump-supply storage?

options.A: I will keep my insulin and pump supplies in my carry-on luggage and protect the insulin from extreme heat and freezing.
options.B: I will pack all insulin in checked luggage because cargo storage keeps medication at a controlled temperature.
options.C: I will place insulin directly against frozen ice packs because freezing does not affect insulin potency.
options.D: I only need the exact amount of insulin for the planned travel time because delays do not affect supply planning.

rationale: A is correct. FDA guidance for insulin-pump travel advises packing pump supplies, including insulin, in carry-on luggage rather than checked baggage because checked items can be delayed, lost, or damaged. FDA insulin-storage guidance also warns that extreme temperatures reduce insulin effectiveness and specifically states not to use insulin that has been frozen and to keep it away from direct heat and sunlight. C is therefore unsafe. B falsely assumes checked baggage protects medication. D ignores FDA travel guidance to plan adequate medication and supplies for possible travel delays.
educational_objective: When traveling with insulin-pump therapy, keep insulin and essential pump supplies in carry-on luggage, protect insulin from extreme heat and freezing, and plan enough medication and equipment for possible delays.
source_document_title: Insulin Pumps: Tips for Using Your Insulin Pump at Home; Information Regarding Insulin Storage and Switching Between Products in an Emergency
source_locator: FDA Insulin Pumps, ‘Traveling with your insulin pump — Airplane travel’: always pack pump supplies, including insulin, in carry-on luggage; Foreign travel: plan enough medicine for trip and delays and review storage requirements. FDA Insulin Storage and Effectiveness: extreme temperatures reduce effectiveness; avoid freezing; do not use frozen insulin; keep away from direct heat and sunlight
source_claim_supported: Air travelers using insulin pumps should carry insulin and pump supplies in carry-on luggage, plan for travel delays, and protect insulin from extreme heat and freezing because temperature extremes can reduce potency.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies; provide client education for safe medication storage, administration devices, and continuity of therapy
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — safe insulin storage and pump-supply planning during travel
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source travel question around current FDA guidance and reclassified it from infection control to Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies. The final item is limited to an insulin-pump traveler, for whom FDA explicitly recommends carry-on packing, and uses FDA temperature-storage precautions without inventing cargo-hold temperature assumptions.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current FDA pump-travel and insulin-storage guidance. The original broad checked-luggage temperature claim was narrowed to explicit FDA recommendations.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A combines direct FDA carry-on and temperature-protection advice. No specific insulin product storage duration or temperature range was generalized across products.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; matches FDA travel and storage guidance.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; FDA advises carrying pump supplies including insulin in carry-on rather than checked luggage.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; frozen insulin should not be used.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; FDA advises planning medication and supplies for possible delays.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A contains the complete safe travel plan; other choices conflict with explicit FDA guidance.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are practical travel-planning statements.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies is the appropriate primary category because the construct is medication/device storage and continuity, not infection prevention.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked carry-on scope, pump-specific wording, extreme-temperature effects, freezing, extra supplies, checked-baggage rationale, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
